scope: Compare purchase due-date input at receipt against later invoice due-date edit across WinUI, API request, server route and infrastructure handler; selected from unmatched semantic-search leads.
decision: The WinUI reuses one TryParseDueDate parser for both receipt-time and later-edit flows: blank maps to null; nonblank must exactly match yyyy-MM-dd invariant format. Receipt sends the parsed nullable DateOnly in ReceivePurchaseRequest. Later edit sends SetPurchaseDueDateRequest via PUT; server replaces body PurchaseId with route id, then handler resolves ActorUserId, authorizes purchasing_manage, loads the purchase, no-ops on unchanged date, otherwise updates DueDate, appends an audit event, and saves. This is intentional separation of creation and post-receipt term correction; there is no client/server date parsing divergence or money movement in the due-date handler. No new finding.
finding_candidate: None; comparison records parity and no material defect observed.

manual_reasoning.input: TryParseDueDate is a single shared client method called by both receipt and due-date edit, accepts blank as null and uses invariant exact yyyy-MM-dd otherwise. This keeps client UI semantics aligned.
manual_reasoning.server: The receipt handler stores request.DueDate at initial purchase creation as one invoice field. The separate edit handler is authorized and audit logged, but changes only DueDate and no money/account balance. Program route binds URL ID by overwriting PurchaseId in body before calling handler.
manual_reasoning.differences: Creation receives manager approval workflow where required and records purchase/tender/stock; later date edit uses purchasing_manage authorization and audited metadata change only. These are intentionally different lifecycle commands, not divergent financial settlement mirrors.
manual_reasoning.counterevidence: No evidence that past dates are disallowed; do not infer a business requirement. No unauthenticated endpoint conclusion from Program excerpt; auth middleware/policy must be reviewed in its own scope.
manual_reasoning.tests: Parser blank/format boundaries; receipt persists null/date; update persists, clears, unchanged no-op, audit previous/new; route ID overrides mismatched body ID; role denial tests. None executed.

recommendation.action: Keep the shared parser and distinct command responsibilities. Future tests should pin route/body identity binding and audit behavior; do not consolidate the receiving and later-edit handlers because the former creates financial and stock entries while the latter only changes terms.
acceptance: Blank means no due date in both UI flows.
Nonblank client input accepts only invariant yyyy-MM-dd.
Later update requires purchasing_manage at handler boundary and creates no treasury/supplier ledger entry.
Route ID is authoritative for target purchase.
No tests or runtime verification claimed.

reviewer: Main coordinator bounded semantic comparison; not independent challenge.
limitations: One focused semantic path from unmatched lexical leads; not exhaustive search of 244 lead paths.
No API or SQL runtime test.
